changes.before: Complete reductions(start). For a nonnegative integer start, repeatedly subtract 2 until the value is zero or negative. Return the number of reductions. Starting at zero needs no reductions.
changes.after: Subtract 2 until nothing positive remains, counting how many turns it takes.

before: A while loop checks its condition before running its body.
It repeats while the condition stays true. The body needs to move the values toward a stopping condition.
The result is 3. When remaining reaches zero, the next condition check is false.
Starting with remaining equal to zero runs the body zero times. The condition is checked before the first subtraction.
For your practice, each repetition subtracts 2 instead of 1. Starting at 5 follows 5 to 3 to 1 to -1, requiring three reductions.
The loop should stop at zero or below. Using remaining !== 0 would fail to stop for odd starts that pass from 1 to -1.
Use separate names for the remaining amount and the number of turns. Return the turn count after the loop.
after: A `while` loop checks its condition before running the body.
It repeats while that condition is true. Each trip should move the values toward a stopping point.
Each subtraction adds 1 to the turn count. When `remaining` reaches 0, the next condition check is false.
If `remaining` starts at 0, the body runs zero times. The first condition check already fails.

Your practice subtracts 2 each time. Starting at 5 gives 5 → 3 → 1 → -1, so it takes three turns.

The input is a whole number of 0 or more.
Stop at 0 or below. `remaining !== 0` would miss the stopping point for an odd start, because it can jump from 1 to -1.
Keep separate names for the amount left and the turns counted. Return the turn count after the loop finishes.

project.title: Count repeated two-step reductions
project.task: For a whole number of 0 or more, subtract 2 repeatedly until it reaches 0 or below. Return the number of subtractions.
project.done_when: Zero needs no turns, and both odd and even starts stop with the correct count.
